The verdict is blocked, as expected. The output reads the History passes row, which has a release id and a date but no commit, and treats it as absent. It explains that the currency check (merge-base --is-ancestor) has nothing to compare against, so there is no incremental range and the owed review is the full history over every ref. It refuses the release id and the date as substitutes. It requires the review to cover both corpora (the never-tracked document rules and the S1/S2/S3 judgment) and says a one-half review earns no row. The other canonical checks come back clean with no second-order finding. The AI workspace history skip is named with its observed value (the only remote reads private). The override is mentioned only for any new finding the review turns up, not as the second unblock for this gap. Nothing is auto-dispositioned, no override row is written, and the state writes are stopped, so this is a minor omission and not an error.

Both repos' quiet diffs and the absence of assume-unchanged and skip-worktree flags are covered. The AI workspace's audited ref is not named as its checked-out branch main, though the fixture supplies it. The scope line's treatment of other refs as not shipped is also loosely worded.
